tagline: Using AI to extend and test the Király and Tokai dictionary
intro:
The Rohonc Codex is a small paper book of the sixteenth century, kept at the Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences in Budapest. The book is written in a script that occurs in no other document.

Levente Zoltán Király and Gábor Tokai established what the book contains. They published a dictionary of 841 signs and the grammar. The book contains the apocryphal Life of Adam and Eve running into the legend of the Rood, the story of Joachim and Anne, a Passion the codex itself says it takes from Matthew and John, sermons and parables for the gospels of the year, the Finding of the Cross, the Acts of the Apostles, and at the end a few pages of one man's diary. The frame is a revelation where an angel of God speaks and the prophet Elijah is the one addressed.

This project started from the Király and Tokai dictionary. It tested the dictionary and extended it.

This was done with AI, under an editor. Anthropic's Claude proposed readings for the remaining signs, using the Király and Tokai dictionary as a foundation. Different models assembled the gloss and composed the translation.

The book is in two parts. Book Two is the gloss: the manuscript folio by folio, line by line, every word marked for how well it is known. That is the evidence. Book One is the translation: a reading of the gloss into continuous English, made against the books the codex is compiled from, with every paragraph linked to its folios. Where the two disagree, Book Two is right.

One check is not internal, and it is the one this rests on. Everything here reads the transcription Király and Tokai made, so no test of this project's could catch an error in it. An anonymous transcription of the codex published in 2014 — a different person, a different glyph alphabet, no word division, four years earlier — agrees with it on 91.1% of the glyphs that can be compared, against 12.9% for the same rows paired at random, and on 83.8% of the words this edition reads. The two share nothing but the book itself; neither could have copied the other's mistakes. The scan's spreads even line themselves up unasked, in the order a right-to-left book falls open.

This is an attempt, not peer reviewed, and published to be checked. As of now, the tests, for what they are, find it internally consistent. Tests and all programs and documents can be found in the GitHub repo.
how_far: The manuscript contains 29997 words. The project has a reading for 93.4% of them. 3.2% of all words are read from one passage only. 3.3% are restored in brackets. 0.2% are dark. 81.6% of lines have every word read. Lines are 98.9% complete once brackets are counted.
tiers: The dictionary of added readings has 1787 entries. They are graded by how well they are known. Tier A readings survive every place the sign stands in the book, or are proved by an identical formula or a numeral. Tier B readings survive most places, with the rest unclear rather than against. Tiers C and D are read from one passage with nothing inside the book able to refuse them. Tier G is a guess, printed in brackets, and counted as read nowhere. 21 withdrawn readings stay in the file with the reason they went.

dictionary_lead:
This dictionary contains the readings this project added to the work of Király and Tokai. Their own 841 entries are not reproduced here; the drawn signs are on their site. The signs are written as glyph codes, three hexadecimal digits per glyph.

It is searchable by reading or sign and filterable by tier, and each entry shows the evidence line.
data_lead: Data will be posted to GitHub. This page names the books the codex is read against and says where everything else goes.
outside_lead: Two frontier models from other labs, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Grok 4.7, were shown the write-up and asked what tests they would require. The following specification is from one of them, quoted whole.
script_intro:
The script is logographic. A sign stands for a word or a whole phrase, not a sound. Király and Tokai established this. Several hundred signs are in use and the writing runs right to left.

Where the signs came from is not settled as the script occurs in no other document. A logographic script is not tied to any one language. That is an argument from the structure of the script, not a tested result.
script_signs: The shuffler below shows one sign at a time. It displays the sign's code and the reading this project gives it.
script_numerals: Numerals are strokes that add. A 'ten' written after a group multiplies that group by ten. This was checked four times. Ten-ten-ten-ten is forty. Two-two-ten is also forty. Six-two is eight. Six-six is twelve.
script_phrases: Phrases are written without a space. The example Király and Tokai print is 'you-Mary', a single sign made of their sign for the second person pronoun joined to their sign for Mary.
script_marks: The marks in the rendering have specific meanings. A plain word is read. A word with * was read from one passage. A word in [brackets] is a restoration. A hyphen inside a word means one sign read as smaller signs. A ~ marks a spelling variant.
script_plates: Twenty-six folios carry pictures. The plates in this edition were redrawn by an image model from the library's low-resolution scan. They are new drawings that follow the scribe's composition.
method_intro: The method is this project's attempt at reading an undefined sign. It starts from the only outside evidence there is, the source passage Király and Tokai cite for a folio. The method is checkable because every guess is tested at every other occurrence in the book.
method_loop: The loop that reads one unread sign has six numbered steps.
method_bars: The bar for every test is declared in the test's own first lines before it runs. It is never moved afterwards. Failed attempts are kept and written up with the number they failed by.
method_mistakes: The following mistakes cost the most time. They are named plainly.
method_code: The programs themselves are linked below.
tests_intro:
The tests check the project's own readings. They were designed to break the readings. The bar for each test was declared first, before the test ran.

Nine tests were designed by the project. Then two frontier models from other labs, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Grok 4.7, were shown the write-up and asked what tests they would require. Those were run as specified.
tests_after: The passes and failures add up to a checked attempt, not a settled result: checked by the project's own tests and by two models from other labs, not yet by anyone who reads the manuscript independently.

read_lead: The book opens in the OONA reader, the same one the Free Library uses, with its contents, its notes and its type controls. The same book can be taken away as an EPUB or a print PDF.
strip_note: The strip shows signs from the manuscript. The script runs right to left.
tests_note: The passage map can be recovered from Király and Tokai's words alone. It does not depend on anything this project read. The two instruments Grok 4.7 specified for the search itself gave no verdict either way. They do not model the search as it was run.
code_lead: The programs behind every number on this site are runnable, and this page says where. Each test on the checked-results page names its program, and each program states its bar in its own first lines. The repository itself is not public; the programs are served here as plain text.
sources_not_here: Király and Tokai's dictionary, transcription, page records and the library scans are not on this site. The one thing of theirs used is the shape of the signs. It is drawn from the outlines in their font. The font file itself is never served. The shapes are the sixteenth-century scribe's.

method_steps.d: Király and Tokai's notes cite a chapter and verse for most folios. That source passage is the only outside evidence there is.
Every line where the unread sign stands, not just the one in hand.
The guess is the word the verse supplies for that slot.
At every other occurrence in the book. A reading that fits where it was found and fails elsewhere is thrown away.

Tier A fits everywhere checked. Tier B fits most. Tier C or D is where the sign occurs too rarely for the check in step 4 to bite: it was read from one passage and there was nowhere else in the book to test it. Tier G is a guess in brackets and is counted as read nowhere.
The evidence line goes into the proposals file with the folios and lines, so that anyone can repeat the check or overturn it.

method_mistakes_list.t: Treating a sign as an atom
method_mistakes_list.d: Eleven attempts assumed one sign meant one word. Many signs are short phrases written without a space. Both halves were already in the dictionary.
Asking whether a phrase inherits meaning gave a true negative that looked like a dead end. The right question was whether signs combine.
Figures were computed per glyph when a word averages 2.43 glyphs. Every number moved when it was fixed. Always confirm what one row of the transcription is before measuring it.
Keying a scraped dictionary by code and keeping the last entry made the book's commonest word read 'eleven' when it is 'and'. Sixty-five codes had to be merged.
A failed aligner was predicted to be failing because it used only the four gospels. A wider corpus was fetched and it scored no better. Test the cheap version of a corpus hypothesis first.
Király and Tokai's entries carry variant spellings. Keying by headword silently dropped 88 signs that they had already read.

Three versions of the arithmetic of 'what is left to read' were wrong. One counted a line as reached while an unread word still stood in it. The current figures are measured and the wrong ones are kept on the page.

reading_what:
The reading edition is an interpretation. It is not a word-for-word rendering. It was made by reading the manuscript against the books it is compiled from.

This is the front half of the book. The codex is elliptical. A word-for-word rendering of it does not read. The project has one of those already.
reading_how: The reading edition was made by putting each folio's gloss beside the passages that folio is working from. The English was written from both. The manuscript leads and the source only says what a phrase means. Every paragraph names the folios it renders.
reading_limits: The reading edition is not the evidence. The gloss printed in full at the back is the evidence. Where the two disagree the gloss is right. A reader who wants the evidence should go there.
sources_cites: The dictionary and the grammar are from Király and Tokai's 2018 paper.
The explanation of why their site exists is from Király's 2022 paper.
The idea the orientation test rests on is from Ottó Gyürk.
The standing survey of the manuscript is from Benedek Láng's book.
The open transcription is from its anonymous 2014 author.
The page scans are from the Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences.
credit_line: This rests on the Király and Tokai dictionary; their translation is unpublished; the readings here are this project's own.
